# The time axis' minor row loses a day's name once its start scrolls out

## Context

Seen on `examples/scheduler/zoom` (#21617, PR #21713) at 1440 × 900 on `dev` `f6afbf6be3`. Its Week level keeps Monday 08:00 at the left edge, so Monday's minor tick starts 72 px left of the view and its label is gone. The row reads `08 09 10 …` over Monday's bars. `examples/gantt/zoom` on `dev` has the same week level (days under weeks): scroll the plan half a day and that day's minor label leaves the view with its start.

## The Problem

#20890 made a major tick's label pin to the visible left edge while its tick is partly scrolled out. Minor ticks never got that, because they render their text directly in the tick (`src/timeline/TimeAxisHeader.mjs:789`) rather than in a label node that could stick. At the week level the days are the minor row, so the row the reader scans for "which day is this" is the one that loses the name.

## The Architectural Reality

- Design authority: `resources/css/src/timeline/TimeAxisHeader.css:72`: "A day, week or month whose start is scrolled out keeps its name at the visible left edge". The rule's selector covers only `.neo-timeline-tick-major .neo-timeline-tick-label`, and a day in the minor row is the same promise unkept.
- Major ticks build a `neo-timeline-tick-label` span (`TimeAxisHeader.mjs:772`); minor ticks set `text` on the tick (`:789`). Every tick carries `data-unit` (`:766`, `:783`).
- The header toolbar is the sticky labels' scroll container (`overflow: clip`, `TimeAxisHeader.css:3`).
- An hour must not pin: a pinned `08:00` would mark 08:30.

## The Fix

Minor ticks render their text in the same `neo-timeline-tick-label` span as major ticks. The sticky rule extends to `.neo-timeline-tick-minor` whose `data-unit` is `day`, `week` or `month`. Unit specs that read a minor tick's `text` read its label instead.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] At `examples/gantt/zoom`'s Week level, a day whose start is scrolled out shows its name at the visible left edge of the minor row: red on `dev`, green at head (e2e).
- [ ] An hour's label is not pinned: at the Day level, a scrolled-out hour's label leaves with its tick.
- [ ] Every minor tick renders its text in a `neo-timeline-tick-label` span, and the timeline unit specs pass.
- [ ] No change to major ticks or to the hover from #21702 (PR #21714).

## Out of Scope

Label formats. The header's hover (#21702). A marker for the repeated DST hour.
